outcome: A data-centre fabric where connectivity is declared as policy between application groups instead of hand-edited access lists.
overview: A bank’s data-centre network usually encodes years of decisions in VLANs and access lists that nobody wants to touch, and every new application takes weeks of network change to land. Nexus switching with ACI expresses connectivity as policy between application groups rather than as addresses, so a new application is described once and the fabric implements it. The cost is real and should be stated plainly: the policy model is a genuinely different way of thinking about the network, and teams that do not invest in that shift end up running ACI as expensive VLANs.

benefits.text: Connectivity is expressed as policy between application groups rather than addresses and access lists
benefits.limits: The benefit requires applications to be grouped meaningfully; a one-group-per-VLAN mapping reproduces the old model in new syntax

benefits.text: Provisioning a new application’s connectivity becomes a policy change rather than a change programme
benefits.limits: Change approval, not fabric configuration, is often the longer pole in a bank; measure both or the improvement will be attributed to the wrong place

benefits.text: The fabric’s intended state is explicit, so drift and undocumented paths become visible
benefits.limits: Visibility of the fabric is not visibility of everything; anything bridged around it stays invisible and should be identified in assessment

residency: Fabric and controller run entirely inside the bank’s own data centres; no fabric state or telemetry leaves the estate

notFor.situation: A data centre already running a policy fabric from another vendor
notFor.why: Two fabrics means two policy models and a long interconnect, which is worse than either alone

notFor.situation: A small data centre with a stable, slowly changing application set
notFor.why: The policy model’s value is in change velocity; where change is rare it is overhead

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco data-centre implementation partner · Duration: 16–24 weeks to a fabric with a first application group in production
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term appropriate to data-centre criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — application dependency observation, existing fabric inventory, growth envelope
2) Design — grouping model, fabric topology, migration waves and the operating-model transition plan
3) Build — spine and leaf fabric, controllers, policy model instantiated
4) Migrate and hand over — first application group in production, network team operating the policy model
deliverables: A new application group is provisioned through policy with no per-switch configuration
The controller reports where running state has diverged from intended state
The grouping model is demonstrably not a one-to-one mapping of the legacy VLAN layout
effort: 16–24 weeks to a fabric with a first application group in production
